spec.name: Reversal v7
spec.notes: Mean reversion of recent returns across names.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.3, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.29 to -0.16 (change -2.45).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.29 to 2.29. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is -0.55 (as submitted, 0 bps: 2.29); it breaks even at 8.1 bps with daily turnover 0.45.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.29 against 2.29 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is -1.58 against 2.29 in research, a gap of +3.87.
The best year gives 19% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 71%; Sharpe is 2.57 in calm and 2.04 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 2.30 becomes 2.30 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.29 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.55).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.29 to as low as 1.89 (as low as 1.89 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 25% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 15% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
